screenings.title: Nenette and Boni
screenings.description: Alice Houri and Grégoire Colin, playing an estranged sister and brother reunited after leaving the same broken home behind, are the title characters of Denis’s domestic drama, a film whose emotional generosity is perfectly matched by the luminous warmth of its images. Nénette, 15 and pregnant, shows up on the doorstep of her brother, a terminally horny 19-year-old line cook at a Marseilles pizzeria, and after initial misgivings, the siblings clumsily try their hand at forming a family. Denis’s first collaboration with the Nottingham group Tindersticks, who would go on to join Jean-Louis Ughetto in the director’s repertory ensemble of professional associates, both parties contributing inestimably to the film’s marvelous, buoyant musicality—as does Brian Wilson, as the Beach Boys’ “God Only Knows” gets an indelible needle drop.

screenings.title: Playtime
screenings.description: On official business in Paris, Tati’s beloved, bumbling alter-ego Monsieur Hulot discovers himself lost in a new, modern cityscape of midcentury modern glass cubes, gimcrack gadgets, squeaky pleather, and shiny chromium. A brilliant burlesque of the Bauhaus future c. 1967, using some of the most elaborate sets ever created for a French film, and an experimental narrative that has the rowdy democratic mob as its ensemble "hero."

screenings.title: Falling Leaves
screenings.description: Iosseliani’s debut feature—winner of the FIPRESCI Award at Cannes—follows newly minted oenologists Nico and Otar, just out of winemaking school, as they head to work at an agricultural cooperative in Tbilisi, there to have their first intimate experiences of the opposite sex… as well as their introduction to the corruption bred by stifling bureaucracy and arbitrarily imposed production quotas. A stinging satire of Soviet-style economic planning and its unintended consequences smuggled within a pseudo-documentary depiction of the Georgian wine industry, and a deeply personal film about youth for the first time facing up to the full measure of adult negligence and corruption.

screenings.title: Je Tu Il Elle
screenings.description: Akerman’s boldly minimalistic first feature stars the 24-year-old writer-director herself as a young woman who we see emerging from an existence of isolation. She hitches a ride with a truck driver with whom she has a sexual dalliance, before finally arriving at the home of a former lover, falling into her bed in a bout of joyous lovemaking which, depicted in real-time, is regarded as a landmark depiction of lesbian sex in cinema. “Filmed in an uncomfortably direct yet distanced manner,” Janet Bergstrom wrote in Sight & Sound, the boudoir scene “provided a startling new perspective on voyeurism, exhibitionism, and the woman’s image on screen.”

screenings.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
screenings.description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills. That’s just the start of the orgy of unhinged behavior that makes up Almodóvar’s gaudy, cheeky screwball melodrama about Shiite terrorist cells and romance on the rocks, a camp romp celebration of emotional excess that has all the makings of an obscure cult classic, yet improbably became the highest-grossing Spanish film of all time upon release, and did its part in putting co-star Antonio Banderas on the international stage.

screenings.title: There Once Was a Singing Blackbird
screenings.description: Gia (Gela Kandelaki), a timpanist in the Tbilisi Philharmonic, has made a science of getting to work just on time to hit his lone cue and then dashing out the door, so as to leave the rest of his hours open for sweet-talking women and carousing with pals. A marvelous character study of an open-handed, incurably impulsive young man infected by the bustling, on-the-go energy of the city around him, and a film that careens along with the same freewheeling spontaneity displayed by its protagonist.

screenings.title: After Hours
screenings.description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York without a penny to his name or the means to get back home in Scorsese’s bravura black comedy of class resentment, all-pervasive paranoia, and creeping castration anxiety, in which the director can be briefly spotted manning a spotlight at punk rock dive Club Berlin. As Dick Miller’s diner waiter explains to the hapless Hackett, “Different rules apply when it gets this late…” As true of the city in 1985 as it is today.

screenings.title: Pastorale
screenings.description: A Tbilisi-based string quartet, seeking a quiet place to practice, light out for a mountain village, taking lodgings with the family of a long-haul truck driver and rehearsing on the house’s veranda as, around them, the daily life of the mountain hamlet continues unabated, albeit to an incongruous soundtrack of classical music. The film that marks Iosseliani’s decisive turn towards tales in which a community—or, at any rate, an ensemble—act as protagonist, Pastorale, winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival, is a work of marvelously polished little moments, not another stereotyped city mouse-country mouse culture-clash but something far more elusive, more insightful, and ultimately more affecting.

screenings.title: The Dark Knight
screenings.description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.”

screenings.title: Wake in Fright
screenings.description: It’s the eve of the Christmas holiday, and polite, young middle-class schoolteacher John Grant (Gary Bond), tied to a position at a tiny township in the outback, is on his way to Sydney to see his girlfriend by way of a stopoff in the grubby mining burg Bundanyabba (“The Yabba” to locals) when he pops into the pub for a drink… Five days of debauchery with local degenerates Donald Pleasence and Chips Rafferty later, the fresh-faced Grant has been replaced by a desperate, unshaven, beer-and-booze-pickled maniac, acquainted with species of depravity he could scarcely have imagined a week ago, and with the barbaric rites of the bush. A furious fever dream from Canuck director Kotcheff, who knew a thing or two about chronic self-degradation as practiced in far-flung outposts of the British Commonwealth, and one of the greatest of Australian films.

screenings.title: Jennifer's Body
screenings.description: High school besties Anita and Jennifer (Amanda Seyfried and Megan Fox) are all but inseparable—though “Needy” Anita is a mousy bookworm and Jennifer a lusted-after member of the color guard—but can their opposites-attract dynamic survive Jennifer’s transformation into a succubus with an insatiable appetite for the flesh of their male classmates? A celebration of the pleasures of camp, kink, and practical gore effects that moves at sleek screwball feed thanks to Diablo Cody’s rat-a-tat screenplay, Kusama’s brisk direction, and the on-a-dime comic timing of its leads. (Not to speak of the redoubtable Amy Sedaris, as Anita’s perpetually disheveled, out-to-lunch mother.)

screenings.title: Troy
screenings.description: Before The Odyssey there was The Iliad, and before Christopher Nolan’s sword-and-sandals smash there was Troy, Petersen’s rather free adaptation of Homer (with a smidge of Quintus Smyrnaeus’s Posthomerica for flavor.) Orlando Bloom’s Paris lures the lovely Helen (Dianne Kruger) away from her throne in Sparta to the city of Troy, and so launches a thousand ships from the Peloponnese hellbent on dragging her back, among those aboard the fabled warrior Achilles (Brad Pitt) and the cunning strategist Odysseus (Sean Bean), soon to test their mettle against Trojan champion Hector (Eric Bana) and his armies. A strapping slab of impassioned spectacle, opulent production design, and earnest romanticism which, though critically divisive on its initial release, has in recent months seen the ranks of its admirers swell.

screenings.title: Brazil
screenings.description: Ground into despairing dust by his routine as a low-level bureaucrat in an Orwellian near-future—drabulously conceived as a junk shop jumble by art directors Norman Garwood and Maggie Gray—Sam (Jonathan Pryce) takes flight only in his imagination, where he plays the winged savior to distressed damsel Kim Griest. A chance teleprinter error at work and a wrongful arrest, however, set Sam on a course for real adventure, one involving his dream girl’s truck-driving double, a suspected terrorist (Robert De Niro), a freakshow cocktail party, plastic surgery disasters, and much more outlandishness besides. “A melancholy, joke-ridden view of the horribleness of where we are now and the worst horribleness of where we’re heading… It’s like a stoned, slapstick 1984: a nightmare comedy in which the comedy is just an aspect of the nightmarishness.” —Pauline Kael, The New Yorker

screenings.title: Peking Opera Blues
screenings.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.”

screenings.title: Don't Play with Fire
screenings.description: Tsui’s outraged and outrageous third feature is a raw, tormented howl of hopeless rebellion that follows a trio of endorphin-addicted, bomb-planting teen nihilists as they get themselves involved with Triad thugs, gun runners, and—most perilous of all—a young woman (Lin Chen-chi) with a penchant for torturing small animals. Shredded by Hong Kong censors who blanched at its bloody-mindedness and its employment of shocking images from the city’s 1967 riots, Don’t Play with Fire (aka Dangerous Encounters of the First Kind) can be seen in a new restoration supervised by the director himself. An open provocation to anarchic upheaval, the blistering heat of its anti-establishment rage undiminished through the years.

screenings.title: Uncut Gems
screenings.description: Adam Sandler gives a career-best performance as Howard Ratner, a fast-talking jeweler in Manhattan’s Diamond District with a penchant for living on the edge and well beyond his means, in the Safdies’ hectic, often hilarious thriller, where a debt-saddled Howie makes a series of high-stakes parlay bets on Kevin Garnett’s performance in the 2012 NBA playoffs that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime—or the abrupt end of his gambling career. “It’s gritty, but in the ’80s sense of it—gritty, with a lot of light and contrast. I started being a cinematographer in the ’80s, so they went back to this period of time where we were after very strong, ink blacks, very long lenses, very contrast-y images, very harsh contours… It was completely unlike anything I’ve done. I would never have thought I would photograph one day a movie like this. But it ended up being my favorite work, probably.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: The Sandwich Man
screenings.director: Hou Hsiao-hsien, Tseng Chuang-hsiang, Wan Jen
screenings.description: A foundational text of the Taiwanese New Wave, omnibus triptych The Sandwich Man represented a clean break from the cloying sentimentality of most of the country’s studio product, with director’s Hou, Wan, and Tseng each adapting stories from a collection by Huang Chung-ming and addressing, with bracing directness, the harsh realities of contemporary urban life. Hou bats leadoff with the devastating namesake segment, about a man eking out a living as a human advertising board; Tseng’s Vickie’s Hat offers a cautionary tale about the perils of modern convenience, namely imported Japanese pressure cookers; Wan’s The Taste of Apples acquaints us with a family in the Taipei City slums whose only hope for a glimpse of the good life is a bed in the American Navy hospital.

screenings.title: Stealing Beauty
screenings.description: After the death of her poet mother, 19-year-old American Lucy (Liv Tyler) travels to a Tuscan villa near Siena owned by family friends in hopes of exploring her family’s history and reuniting with her first kiss, though soon finds herself contending with a crowded field of would-be suitors. Working in his native Italy for the first time in 15 years, and in his only collaboration with DP Darius Khondji, Bertolucci creates a film of warm, mellow light; lyrical grace notes; and exquisite performances from Tyler, Joseph Fiennes, Jeremy Irons, Rachel Weisz, and others.

screenings.title: Don't Play with Fire
screenings.description: Tsui’s outraged and outrageous third feature is a raw, tormented howl of hopeless rebellion that follows a trio of endorphin-addicted, bomb-planting teen nihilists as they get themselves involved with Triad thugs, gun runners, and—most perilous of all—a young woman (Lin Chen-chi) with a penchant for torturing small animals. Shredded by Hong Kong censors who blanched at its bloody-mindedness and its employment of shocking images from the city’s 1967 riots, Don’t Play with Fire (aka Dangerous Encounters of the First Kind) can be seen in a new restoration supervised by the director himself. An open provocation to anarchic upheaval, the blistering heat of its anti-establishment rage undiminished through the years.

screenings.title: Games of Love and Loneliness
screenings.description: Adapted from the novel A Serious Game by Swedish author Hjalmar Söderberg, whose play Gertrud had been the source for Carl Theodor Dreyer’s final film of the same title, Games of Love and Loneliness stars Stefan Ekman as Arvid, a young newspaperman who prioritizes professional ambitions over personal considerations so much as to pause his passionate romance with Lydia (Lil Terselius) just shy of wedding vows—complicating matters when the death of her father leaves Lydia in precarious circumstances and open to the prospect of a marriage of convenience. A handsomely mounted and deeply felt period melodrama spanning the years between 1897 and 1912, redolent with regret concerning opportunities not seized and roads not taken.

screenings.title: Orpheus
screenings.description: Cocteau’s lushly lyric, allegorical update of the Orpheus myth, based on his play of the same title, depicts a famous poet (Jean Marais) who’s scorned by the Left Bank youth, torn between his love for his wife, Eurydice (Marie Déa), and a mysterious, black-clad princess (Maria Casarès). Seeking inspiration, the poet follows the princess from the world of the living to the land of the dead, a dreamlike journey that begins with his passage through Cocteau’s famous mirrored portal, one of the film’s several enchanting low-budget effects.

screenings.title: Wives: Ten Years After
screenings.description: Frøydis Armand, Katja Medbøe, and Anne Marie Ottersen return as Heidrun, Kaja, and Mie, 10 years older and another decade removed from youth’s relative freedom from responsibility. Each of the trio have been molded by years of cohabitation in ways that their friends see more clearly than themselves, all determined to keep the spree going after meeting at a pre-Christmas party, hiding out from their families in an otherwise empty Malmö hotel whose manager provides them obsequious service. By turns somber and irreverent, with Nils Vogt and Jon Eikemo very funny in supporting turns, and the three leads the very definition of ensemble chemistry.

screenings.title: Black Orpheus
screenings.description: Winner of the Palme d’Or at Cannes and the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, Camus’s international arthouse smash transposes the legend of Orpheus and Eurydice to the favelas of Rio de Janeiro and sets the proceedings shimmying along to a bossa nova beat courtesy composers Antônio Carlos Jobim and Luiz Bonfá. Intoxicating in its zestful, go-for-the-gusto vitality, with Breno Mello charming in the title role and Marpessa Dawn every bit as appealing as the ill-fated beloved he’s determined to follow into the underworld. “An almost irrationally infectious retelling of the Orpheus-Eurydice chestnut set during carnival and feverish with hip-swiveling hustle, exploding local color, and sleeve-worn heart.” —The Village Voice

screenings.title: Wives III
screenings.description: A surprise 50th birthday party for Kaja (Katja Medbøe) thrown on a city streetcar by old school chums Heidrun and Mie (Frøydis Armand and Anne Marie Ottersen) turns into another conversational bender in the third entry of Breien’s very singular franchise, in which the pleasure the central trio take in one another’s company is very much contagious. Deferred dreams, children reaching the cusp of adulthood, aging parents on the verge of the hereafter, husbands and lovers—it’s all grist for the mill in this wry, wistful, and very moving capstone to the trilogy, with Oslo’s Independence Day providing a jubilant background to their final round of playing hooky.

screenings.title: Dust in the Wind
screenings.description: Young lovers Wan and Huen, fresh out of junior high school in the remote, mountainous mining town where they were raised, look forward to a bright future together in their new home of Taipei—only to face first the grim reality of urban life there, then a three-year separation, after Wan is drafted into the Republic of China Army, which ultimately proves fatal to their affections. Based on the personal experiences of frequent Hou co-screenwriter Wu Nien-jen, the poignant, plangent Dust in the Wind has emerged as a popular favorite among Hou’s films, his first collaboration with composer Chen Ming-chang and actor Li Tian-lu, which also features some of Mark Lee Ping-bing’s most hypnotically beautiful tracking shots.

screenings.title: I Want Your Sex
screenings.description: In the latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Araki (“Mysterious Skin”), I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twenty-something whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli xcx) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery and murder through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is known.
screenings.country: I Want Your Sex Romance, Thriller

screenings.title: Office Space
screenings.description: A household name thanks to the runaway success of MTV’s Beavis and Butthead, Judge made the leap into live-action filmmaking with this cult comedy of white-collar alienation, inspired by his 1991 animated short. Cubicle jockey Peter (Ron Livingston) checks out of his soul-sucking job for good after an encounter with an “occupational hypnotherapist” gone awry, only to have his superiors, impressed by his new air of utter indifference, pelt him with promotion after promotion. A wryly wicked satire about corporate culture and its gangsta rap-loving discontents.

screenings.title: Rebels of the Neon God
screenings.description: Tsai’s first theatrically released film isn’t as pared down in its approach as some of his later works—it even has a rather catchy synth theme song!—but in most respects it’s pure Tsai, a film about urban loners and the city’s (largely unfulfilled) promises of connection and sexual intimacy. Lee Kang-sheng, Tsai’s acteur fétiche, stars as a teenaged Taipei arcade rat who develops an obsession with a young petty hoodlum (Chen Chao-jung) that’s a tangle of vengeful wrath and repressed lust. An extraordinary debut, in which aspects of all its maker’s films to come are visible.

screenings.title: 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour
screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Ghost World
screenings.description: The story of neo-cool Enid (Thora Birch) and Rebecca (Scarlett Johansson) who, faced with graduation from high school, take a hard look at the world they wryly observe and decide what they really want. When Enid takes an interest in the offbeat Seymour (Steve Buscemi) and Rebecca focuses her attention on their mutual romantic fixation Josh (Brad Renfro), the girls’ friendship is forever changed.

screenings.title: National Theatre Live: Les Liaisons Dangereuses
screenings.description: Marquise de Merteuil is a master in the art of survival. Alongside the magnetic Vicomte de Valmont, they turn seduction into strategy and weaponise desire. But when their alliance collapses into rivalry, the battle between them threatens to destroy everyone in their path.

screenings.title: Union County
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: A Clockwork Orange
screenings.description: “A merciless, demoniac satire in the future imperfect. It posits a world somehow gone berserk, in which there are no real alternatives, only degrees of madness. Kubrick makes the whole thing (as he did in Dr. Strangelove) chillingly and often hilariously believable…. Malcolm McDowell is sensational. His performance has the range and dynamism that signal the arrival of a new superstar. As for Director Kubrick, his work is stylistically almost flawless. If there was any doubt after 2001, A Clockwork Orange confirms Kubrick as our most audacious film maker. There have been many visions of a malign future on film (1984, Things to Come, Fahrenheit 451) but none quite so unsparing and so ruthlessly witty.” – Jay Cocks, TIME

screenings.title: Body Heat
screenings.description: Lawrence Kasdan’s tramped up and ruthless remix of Double Indemnity, sees a Florida heat-wave fry the brain of a dopey two-bit lawyer who falls into the trap of a bored and wealthy woman just out to pass the time while her husband’s out of town with a bit of a steamy affair. As the clothes shed and the days pass, a plot hatches to kill her husband and make off with his mountain of money. Dopey lawyer being what he is, goes for it; but one can hardly blame him, it’s for Kathleen Turner, after all.

screenings.title: Stop Making Sense
screenings.description: Considered by critics as the greatest concert film of all time, STOP MAKING SENSE stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood’s Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads’ most memorable songs.

screenings.title: Evita
screenings.description: Don’t cry for her, Argentina—after years of dauntless campaigning, Madonna landed the coveted role of actress-cum-First Lady Eva Perón in this lavish, costume-change-a-minute adaptation of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber’s 1978 stage musical, featuring Jonathan Pryce as the statesman who shares his power and his bed with Eva, and Antonio Banderas as narrator of her meteoric rise and tragic end. “Evita is actually a very visual movie, and Alan Parker is probably one of the most exciting and visual directors I have ever worked with… He wanted to make the film look very real, almost like a newsreel, but also very glamorous at the same time… There were certain scenes where we had up to 4,000 or 5,000 extras, because Alan didn’t want to use any special effects—he wanted it all to be in front of the lens.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is due for resurrection. And one young director is more than up to the task. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, delirium — under threat from the spear-wielding Little Death.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film and The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makeku Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

Based on the personal experiences of frequent Hou co-screenwriter Wu Nien-jen, the poignant, plangent Dust in the Wind has emerged as a popular favorite among Hou’s films, his first collaboration with composer Chen Ming-chang and actor Li Tian-lu, which also features some of Mark Lee Ping-bing’s most hypnotically beautiful tracking shots.

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Dreams in Nightmares
screenings.description: Three black queer femmes in their mid 30s take a road trip across the Midwestern United States in search of their friend who has seemingly disappeared off the grid.

screenings.title: The Rice Dumpling Vendors
screenings.description: With a wife, a mistress, three children, and a business that provides amply for all, Tsi-bing wants for nothing—that is, until his lover convinces him of his wife’s infidelity, breaks up their household, then clears off with all his cash, sending him tumbling down the socioeconomic ladder, taking odd jobs (including that of the film’s title) and striving to win back the spouse he’d foolishly spurned. One of nearly a thousand Taiyu Pian—films in which the characters speak in Taiwanese Minnan or Hokkien—produced in Taiwan between 1955 and 1981, and one of the crowning achievements of Taipei-born Hsin’s hugely prolific career.

screenings.title: Hercules in the Haunted World
screenings.description: Brit bodybuilder Reg Park straps on the sandals and exomis to play Zeus’s swole love child in Bava’s deliciously delirious peplum, co-written by Mondo Cane’s Franco Prosperi, which follows our hulking hero—as well as Theseus and Telemachus—on a perilous mission to save Herc’s lover Princess Deianira, stricken senseless by illness, endeavoring to procure for her a sacred stone from the depths of Hades, home court of Christopher Lee’s sinister Lyco and his zombie hordes. A triumph of resourcefulness over limited resources, rich with Gothic atmosphere, swirling with nigh-psychedelic colors, and offering at every turn ample evidence of cinematographer-turned-director Bava’s consummate mastery of the motion picture apparatus.

screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.title: Fist Church
screenings.description: Every other Sunday we’ll be mining the depths of VHS, VCD, DVD, and the darkest corners of the internet to bring you the wildest post-brunch experience you’re likely to have. So, get faded on Bloody Mary’s (leave the PCP at home) and come kick your feet up while we play fast and loose with the rules and witness people fight hopping vampires, ninjas, swordsmen and more. The movies won’t be announced, but trust us – on this one we wouldn’t steer you wrong.

screenings.title: Franz

Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film and The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makeku Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

The baroquely intricate plot involves a mystic mission into the mountains of Western China in search of legendary twin swords, while Hark himself is on a mission to see how much gonzo action he can fit into a single movie—one that’s breezily accomplished.

An ensemble cast battle royale in which old resentments resurface alongside deep-buried secrets and bouts of blood-on-the-balls bickering alternate with episodes of remorseful self-recrimination, premiered in the main competition at the 32nd Cannes Film Festival.

screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.description: Arranged to marry a rich man, young Ada (Mame Bineta Sane) is crushed when her true love goes missing at sea during a migration attempt — until a miracle reunites them. Winner of the Grand Prix at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, Mati Diop’s haunting feature directorial debut made history as the first film directed by a Black woman to compete for the Palme d’Or. In Wolof, French and English with English subtitles.

Shredded by Hong Kong censors who blanched at its bloody-mindedness and its employment of shocking images from the city’s 1967 riots, Don’t Play with Fire (aka Dangerous Encounters of the First Kind) can be seen in a new restoration supervised by the director himself. An open provocation to anarchic upheaval, the blistering heat of its anti-establishment rage undiminished through the years.

A film of somber beauty, winner of a Special Mention for Historical Reconstruction and a Best Actress prize at the 1981 Venice Film Festival.

screenings.description: So asks the Artist, one of three intertwined paranoiacs in Roger Copeland’s sprawling post-9/11, DIY, Brechtian fever dream. Proposing a twist on the axiom that the urge to destroy is also a creative urge, Copeland’s film suggests that all creativity is paranoid, and all paranoia is creative. It depicts a world that exists in “a state of semiotic arousal, a horniness for meaning.” Taking place in October of 2001, the film cuts between the story of a young girl who thinks the father that walked out on her family might be among the unrecovered dead at Ground Zero; the self-proclaimed BioEvangelist, who, in between compulsively consuming media coverage of the attacks’ aftermath in his basement chemistry lab, plans his own epistolary reckoning; and the aforementioned Artist, who monologues (livestreams?) from his studio about the ways the “death artists” have put art on the defensive.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Practical Magic 2
screenings.description: Practical Magic 2 returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.title: Showgirls | JT Selects: Club Films
screenings.description: Nomi, a young drifter, arrives in Las Vegas to become a dancer and soon sets about clawing and pushing her way to become the top of the Vegas showgirls.

screenings.title: On a String
screenings.description: Isabel (Isabel Hagen) is a young, Juilliard-trained violist still living at home with her parents in the heart of New York City. She’s trying to make a living playing gigs with her friends but when her toxic ex- boyfriend reappears, who also happens to be the Philharmonic’s “newest, hottest cellist,” he informs her of a viola opening in the prestigious orchestra. Nothing can go wrong, right?

Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Uncut Gems
screenings.description: Adam Sandler gives a career-best performance as Howard Ratner, a fast-talking jeweler in Manhattan’s Diamond District with a penchant for living on the edge and well beyond his means, in the Safdies’ hectic, often hilarious thriller, where a debt-saddled Howie makes a series of high-stakes parlay bets on Kevin Garnett’s performance in the 2012 NBA playoffs that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime—or the abrupt end of his gambling career. “It’s gritty, but in the ’80s sense of it—gritty, with a lot of light and contrast. I started being a cinematographer in the ’80s, so they went back to this period of time where we were after very strong, ink blacks, very long lenses, very contrast-y images, very harsh contours… It was completely unlike anything I’ve done. I would never have thought I would photograph one day a movie like this. But it ended up being my favorite work, probably.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: Peking Opera Blues
screenings.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.”

screenings.title: Union County (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: Colony
screenings.description: Horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s (Train to Busan) new zombie thriller stars Gianna Jun as biology professor Se-jeong, who’s thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: On the Town
screenings.description: U.S., 1949 Directed by Gene Kelly and Stanley Donen Screenplay and lyrics by Betty Comden and Adolph Green Starring Gene Kelly, Frank Sinatra, Ann Miller, Betty Garrett, Vera-Ellen, Jules Munshin Music by Leonard Bernstein Approx. 98 min. “New York, New York” warble gobs Gene Kelly, Frank Sinatra, and Jules Munshin throughout their dazzling all-location-shot opening montage, eventually cavorting from the Bronx to the Battery with “Miss Turnstiles” Vera-Ellen, man-hungry cabbie Betty Garrett, and passionate paleontologist Ann Miller. “Despite brutal scissoring of the Comden-Green-Bernstein score, still the great liberating musical of the American cinema.” – David Shipman Presented with support from The Robert Jolin Osborne Endowed Fund for American Classic Cinema of the 1930s, ’40s, and ’50s and The Roy Lichtenstein Foundation Fund

screenings.title: 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour
screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.description: “A merciless, demoniac satire in the future imperfect. It posits a world somehow gone berserk, in which there are no real alternatives, only degrees of madness. Kubrick makes the whole thing (as he did in Dr. Strangelove) chillingly and often hilariously believable…. Malcolm McDowell is sensational. His performance has the range and dynamism that signal the arrival of a new superstar. As for Director Kubrick, his work is stylistically almost flawless. If there was any doubt after 2001, A Clockwork Orange confirms Kubrick as our most audacious film maker. There have been many visions of a malign future on film (1984, Things to Come, Fahrenheit 451) but none quite so unsparing and so ruthlessly witty.” – Jay Cocks, TIME

screenings.title: anyone lived in a pretty how town
Stop Making Sense
screenings.description: Considered by critics as the greatest concert film of all time, STOP MAKING SENSE stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood’s Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads’ most memorable songs.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Who Moves America (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: In an era of deepening inequality, UPS Teamsters stand on the brink of a historic strike. As the deadline looms, WHO MOVES AMERICA shadows UPS workers in New York, Kentucky, California and across the country as they navigate the challenges of building solidarity with their 340,000 co-workers.

screenings.title: On a String
screenings.description: Isabel (Isabel Hagen) is a young, Juilliard-trained violist still living at home with her parents in the heart of New York City. She’s trying to make a living playing gigs with her friends but when her toxic ex- boyfriend reappears, who also happens to be the Philharmonic’s “newest, hottest cellist,” he informs her of a viola opening in the prestigious orchestra. Nothing can go wrong, right?

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: 2026 Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour
screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “A loving and lovely sensibility runs through LATE FAME, a fond and wise understanding of why some people want to become artists without making much art and why other people quit making it altogether.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “[A] lovely and bittersweet drama... Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... In a prolific career filled with complex and striking characters, the role of Ed Saxberger is a subdued but particularly rich one for Dafoe, himself a veteran of the downtown arts scene.” – Sheri Linden, The Hollywood Reporter “LATE FAME is a deliciously acidic examination of the thin line between creative aspiration and pretentious poseurdom.” – Wendy Ide, Screen International

screenings.title: Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Practical Magic 2
screenings.description: Practical Magic 2 returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Who Moves America
screenings.description: In an era of deepening inequality, UPS Teamsters stand on the brink of a historic strike. As the deadline looms, WHO MOVES AMERICA shadows UPS workers in New York, Kentucky, California and across the country as they navigate the challenges of building solidarity with their 340,000 co-workers.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: Kwaidan
screenings.description: Japan, 1964 Directed by Masaki Kobayashi Based on a collection of folktales by Lafcadio Hearn Starring Tatsuya Nakadai, Rentarô Mikuni, Michiyo Aratama, Misako Watanabe Approx. 183 min. Four ghost stories by American expatriate Lafcadio Hearn (1850-1904): When he adds a second wife, Rentarô Mikuni finds a skeleton at the feast; woodcutter Tatsuya Nakadai (star of Kobayashi’s Harakiri and Kurosawa’s Yojimbo and Ran) meets a strange woman in the snow; a blind biwa player gives a command performance for a spirit; an apparition appears in a cup of tea. Kobayashi’s first color film, with an eerie score by the great Tōru Takemitsu (Ran, Harakiri, Teshigahara’s Woman in the Dunes, etc.). Restoration by Toho Co., Ltd. Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film and The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makeku Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: The Night is Short, Walk on Girl
screenings.description: A surreal nocturnal animated odyssey from Yuasa, the mad genius behind Mind Game, rendered in a frenetic, galaxy-brained, endlessly morphing style. The Night is Short, Walk on Girl follows a mysterious high schooler known only as The Girl with Black Hair through the streets of Kyoto’s famed Ponto-Cho party district, drinking middle-aged salarymen under the table when she’s not mixing with barflies, obsessive collectors, and guerilla theater performers, all the while oblivious to the efforts of a fellow student who has been creating increasingly fantastic and contrived reasons to run into her in a gambit to win her love. A comic fable of fleeting youthful passions, as lived out through one mad, unforgettable night.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: Old Joy
screenings.description: Two boyhood pals who have since drifted apart, played by Daniel London and musician Will Oldham, impulsively reunite for a camping and hiking trip in the verdant woods of the Pacific Northwest in Reichardt’s breakout sophomore feature, released 12 years after debut River of Grass. Dialogue is at a minimum in Reichardt’s serene, solemn film, but London and Oldham’s taciturn, intricately detailed performances—as well as the plangent score by Yo La Tengo and the evocative photographing of the landscape—speak volumes about middle-aged mournfulness and faded friendship. Distributor: Janus Films

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.title: Live and Let Die
screenings.description: When James Bond (Roger Moore) investigates the murders of three fellow agents, he finds himself a target, evading vicious assassins as he closes in on powerful Kananga (Yaphet Kotto). Known on the streets as Mr. Big, Kananga is coordinating a global threat, using tons of self-produced heroin. As Bond tries to unravel the mastermind’s plan, he meets Solitaire (Jane Seymour), a beautiful tarot-card reader, whose magic is crucial to the crime lord.

screenings.title: The Apartment
screenings.description: Jack Lemmon is one anxious face in a sea of stooges at the New York insurance company where he toils, a passive nobody able to distinguish himself to his superiors only by letting boss Fred MacMurray use his shoebox apartment as a love nest, while his tentative romance with an elevator operator (Shirley MacLaine) plays out against a backdrop of boozy office Christmas parties, mocking holiday decorations, and mirthless cheer. Oh, and it’s a howl, too! The razor-sharp script by Wilder and I.A.L. Diamond gives the film its acerbic slice, while Joseph LaShelle’s elegant, cool black-and-white photography and the brittle tinkle of Adolf Deutsch’s jazz lounge score bring out the underlying sadness of this brilliantly bittersweet paradigm of the comedy-drama.

screenings.title: Farewell, Home Sweet Home
screenings.description: Perhaps the best-loved of Iosseliani’s French productions and the one that earned him the enormously prestigious Prix Louis Delluc, deliciously deadpan formalist comedy Farewell, Home Sweet Home is another of the director’s ensemble narratives, its seemingly disparate, blackout sketch-style segments slowly revealed to be puzzle pieces that form a panorama of high- and lowlife in contemporary Paris. Among the curious characters who flit by is a dissolute upper-class house husband, played by Iosseliani, content to hole up with a bottle and his electric trains while his wife entertains company—a telling image, as the filmmaker here is something like the engineer of a magnificent model train set, transferring from one narrative line to another in some of the most exquisite tracking shots you will ever see.

screenings.title: National Theatre Live: Les Liaisons Dangereuses
screenings.description: Marquise de Merteuil is a master in the art of survival. Alongside the magnetic Vicomte de Valmont, they turn seduction into strategy and weaponise desire. But when their alliance collapses into rivalry, the battle between them threatens to destroy everyone in their path.

screenings.title: Who Moves America

As the deadline looms, WHO MOVES AMERICA shadows UPS workers in New York, Kentucky, California and across the country as they navigate the challenges of building solidarity with their 340,000 co-workers.

screenings.title: Coyote vs. Acme
screenings.description: After decades of being blown to bits by bombs, demolished by dynamite, mangled by magnets, battered by boulders, trampled by trains, tricked by tunnels, sprung by springs, steamrolled by steamrollers, maligned by misfires, bedeviled by bungees, rattled by rockets, backstabbed by bat suits, rocked by rocket skates, upended by unicycles, quaked by quake pills, rubberized by rogue bands, and hurled headlong off every cliff in the Southwest, Wile E. Coyote (Genius) finally fights back. Teaming up with billboard accident lawyer Kevin Avery (Will Forte), he takes on slick corporate counsel Buddy Crane (John Cena) and ACME, Inc., the profit-obsessed conglomerate behind every one of the Coyote’s chaotic catastrophes.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: Crash | Sex, Death, Cars!
screenings.description: Crash is about the strange lure of the auto collision, provoking as it does the human fascination with death and the tendency to eroticize danger. Most motorists will slow down to stare at the scene of a collision they may feel their pulses quickening and become aware of the fragility of their own bodies. The characters of Crash carry this awareness a step further, cherishing and nurturing it. For them, a car collision is a sexual turn-on, and a jolting life force they come to crave.

screenings.title: 9/11, Pgm 3: Circling Zero
screenings.description: The attacks were encoded in the national memory over seemingly endless minutes, hours, days, weeks, and months of media coverage. A quarter of a century later, it is tempting to think of 9/11 as a media event announcing material reality’s final, total subordination to the image—as Baudrillard said, “They did it. We wished it.” Yet to conceive of 9/11 in only these terms would be to overlook the lived horrors of the day and the insidious reverberations of a nationwide psychic trauma. From our historical vantage, the events of September 11 seem as fundamental to our current reality as the air we breathe. In recognition of the twenty-fifth anniversary of September 11, 2001, Spectacle presents a selection of films that confront the phenomenal and psychic impact of the attacks, and the indelible scar they left on the world. There was before, and this is after. Program 1: REICHSTAG 9/11 & DISINTEGRATION LOOP 1.1 REICHSTAG 9/11 Dir. Ken Jacobs, 2016. United States. 38 min. Silent.
